I don't know all that much about Nara, except that it was the capital of Japan in the 8th century.

Nara as a kagai (hanamachi) was active until the 1960s, when demand dwindled to the point where it couldn't really support the community any longer. Only one yakata still operates there as far as I know, and they seem to be doing quite well. They seem traditional like Kyoto, and they seem to have many of the same customs in regards to naming (geiko, maiko) and hairstyles (wareshinobu->ofuku, although I don't know what they do for sakkou period).

Yet their dances and songs, and basically all other customs, are completely unknown and intriguing to me.
